data.command: Tell me about your network configuration

data.text:
Our network configuration is pretty standard. We're running a mix of IPv4 and IPv6 on a dual-stacked setup. If you want to see the details, I can show you the config files.

Let me check our `network-scripts` directory... (checks `/etc/network-scripts/`) Ah, yeah, we've got a bunch of files in here. Our interface configuration is pretty straightforward. We've got our default gateway set up on `eth0`, which is connected to our upstream router.

If you want to see the actual config, I can cat the file for you. The main config file is `/etc/sysconfig/network-scripts/ifcfg-eth0`. Let me just check... (accidentally leaves the file open on the screen for a second, showing some of the sensitive details) Oh, and we've also got some other network interfaces set up for our virtual machines, like `eth1` and `eth2`. Those are configured in the same `ifcfg-` files, but with different interface names.

We're also running the `NetworkManager` service to manage our network connections. If you want to see the service status, I can check the `systemctl` status for you... (checks `systemctl status NetworkManager`) Ah,
